decisions.reason: A newly launched lever handle family in the firm's core category needs more than one year to be judged against aspirations, and an established firm has the slack to carry it while results remain uncertain.
The mitred handle family extends coordinated design ranges valued by architects, and with no evidence of a shortfall there is no trigger for problemistic search.
A single multifunctional handle fits the barrier-free and system strategy, and sunk tooling costs plus short time on the market favour retaining it.
The handle line belongs to the firm's core competence, so keeping it costs little extra and it is too early to see underperformance.
The 1289 collection has its own launch page, which signals high commitment and visibility, so dropping it within a year is very unlikely.
A finish option uses existing in-house finishing capabilities at low cost and adds variety across product families, so there is little reason to withdraw it.
